In sender mode it can read from DIP switches or a 4-button PMOD keypad, and in receiver mode it drives an LCD display value from the received bits. results.summary_before: This Verilog design is a sequencer for a 9-step 4-phase combined power-clock supply intended for adiabatic circuits, running at 32 MHz with each phase at 1/32 of that rate. It generates control signals for phases 0 and 1, with a select pin routing one phase to the output pins, and also provides digital sync signals for latching data into or out of adiabatic gates. The project is free-running: after a reset, the user selects a phase and monitors the outputs. No external hardware is necessary, and the design is explicitly a test of the power supply sequencer concept.

results.summary_before: TinyWSPR is a Chisel-based WSPR beacon that transmits Weak Signal Propagation Reporter radio signals, recommended for the 20m and 40m bands. Configuration is loaded one byte at a time over the config pins, covering callsign, grid square, power level, symbol time, divisor and deviation, after which the RF start pin triggers transmission at the correct time. An external lowpass filter is absolutely required to remove harmonics from the square-wave transmitter, along with a properly tuned antenna. The design is notable for putting a complete WSPR encoder and transmitter into a small digital block, but no silicon test results are reported.
